title: The minimum number of distinct abelian squares in a binary circular word: paper, Lean 4 formalization and verification code
description:
Every binary circular word of length n contains at least floor((n-1)/2) distinct abelian squares, and the words attaining this bound are the conjugates of a^n, b^n, a^{n-1}b, b^{n-1}a for odd n, and of a^k b^{n-k} with k odd, together with (ab)^{n/2} when n = 2 (mod 4), for even n. This settles Conjecture 0.6 of J. Simpson, Solved and unsolved problems about abelian squares (arXiv:1802.04481): part (a) holds, and the list of extremal words in part (b) misses (ab)^{n/2} for n = 2 (mod 4), n >= 6.

preprintSimpsonCircularAbelianSquares/ holds the paper as a PDF; paper/ holds the LaTeX source in the Elsevier elsarticle template with its figures; dist/ holds the PDF, the LaTeX source zip and the arXiv tarball, and MasterSimpsonCircularAbelianSquares_masterzipfinal2.zip holds every file of the repository. verification/lean/ is a Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of the theorem (13 files); its six main theorems depend only on the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. verification/ also contains independent checks in C (every word of length at most 22), C++ (every necklace of length at most 28), Python, Julia and Bash, and scripts/run_all.sh runs the Lean build, the axiom check and all programs.
